chunks: Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the man who enters into Ihram in a dirty garment. He said: 'No,' and I do not say it is forbidden, but I prefer that he purify it, and its purification is washing it. And the man should not wash the garment in which he is in Ihram until he is free from Ihram, even if it becomes dirty, except if sexual impurity touches it or something [else requiring washing], then he should wash it.

key_terms.جَنَابَةٌ: sexual impurity (major ritual impurity requiring full body wash)
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: enters into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing Ihram clothes while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between strict prohibition and recommended etiquette (istihbab) regarding cleanliness in Ihram, emphasizing that the garment's state does not invalidate the pilgrimage status itself. The ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor impurities do not necessitate immediate washing if it risks altering the garment's fit or causing unnecessary hardship, except in cases of major ritual impurity (janabah) or specific soiling that requires purification.
